comment: The bars ci/trees-figures.py holds the tree views' release figures to: the recording engine's budgets (ci/bench-budget.json, docs/performance.md). Advisory: a missed bar is a warning, never a failure. Every workload has its own `deadline_s` and reports what it reached by then; nothing is extrapolated. A workload misses its bar when it does not finish by its deadline, or when its `metric` is over `max` (one number, or one per filesystem). `create` runs for half the engine's 600 s and is held to half its 100,000 creates, the engine's rate of 6 ms a create. `close_64m` is held, unscaled, to the engine's close of a dirty 1 GiB file, and `close_1g` to the same, at its size: the close and stat after the writes. `write_1g` holds the same run's last 64 writes to 1.5 times a 1 MiB file's write. `history_1g` holds that save's drain to 60 s, the engine's own 1 GiB commit (23 to 29 s) with margin, and `memory_1g` the view process's peak memory through it to 256 MiB over its memory before, whatever the file's size. `grace_s` is how long a save the deadline caught may run on before the view's connection is aborted.

close_64m.text: within the engine's close of a dirty 1 GiB file, 12 s on ext4 and 8 s on XFS (bigclose)

close_1g.text: the engine's close of a dirty 1 GiB file, 12 s on ext4 and 8 s on XFS (bigclose, dirty)

history_1g.text: the 1 GiB save built within 60 s of its close (the engine's own 1 GiB commit takes 23 to 29 s)

memory_1g.text: the view's peak memory through the 1 GiB save and its build under 256 MiB over its memory before

write_1g.text: the last 64 1 MiB writes of a 1 GiB file, median within 1.5 times a 1 MiB file's write
